title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: The Eye of Argonia is the old priest-kings' jewel. It sits at the Root, under the sea below Teku-Sul Spire, where the roots of every Hist meet; used there, it can heal every sick tree. The last king shut it behind the Kings' Gate, which opens only with three seal-stones. I carry all three seal-stones of the kings' gate. I'm to bring them to Never-Writes-Twice, who stands at the back of Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom.
objectives: Bring the three seal-stones to Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House, Helstrom. (marker: Never-Writes-Twice)

plan.going: The Eye of Argonia, the old kings' jewel, sits at the Root under Teku-Sul, where the roots of every Hist meet; used there it heals every sick tree. Bring the three seal-stones to Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka House, Helstrom.

title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice made me a Ka-Deelith, a War-Teacher of the Toh-Reel-Ka, and gave me the order's pike. Her watchers have not seen the Unbound near Teku-Sul, so I am ahead of them. I'm to dive to Teku-Sul Spire, open the Kings' Gate with the three stones and use the Eye where it sits to heal the trees. Then I'm to bring the stones back to her and hunt down Cuts-the-Old-Knot.
objectives: Dive to Teku-Sul Spire and go to the Kings' Gate. (marker: The Kings' Gate)

plan.going: I am a Ka-Deelith now. The order thinks I am ahead of the Unbound and has sent me to open the gate and heal the trees with the Eye; afterwards the stones go back to Never-Writes-Twice and I hunt Cuts-the-Old-Knot

title: At the Kings' Gate
journal: Cuts-the-Old-Knot waited before the Kings' Gate without stones, and told me what the order I serve is. The Toh-Reel-Ka are the secret warriors of the Xeech-Leel, the party that rules Black Marsh, made so that no tree could bring another Umbriel. They keep dreamers in the cellar of Fort Chalkmoth: people fed sap and made to tell what the trees have seen, so the order sees the whole marsh. She was a dreamer for nine years, and Never-Writes-Twice kept the key. She seals the trees she drains so the dreamers cannot see through them. Used where it sits, the Eye heals every tree, and the dreamers see through them all again; lifted, it parts the trees, about three in ten die, and the dreams end. If I fight her, I take her tomes, staff and draughts, face the guardian alone, and cannot give her the Eye. If I believe her, she fights the guardian beside me and giving her the Eye stays open. Either way the choice at the Eye is mine. I'm to choose.
objectives: Fight Cuts-the-Old-Knot, or believe her. (marker: Cuts-the-Old-Knot)

plan.going: The Toh-Reel-Ka are the secret warriors of the Xeech-Leel, the party that rules Black Marsh; they were made so that no tree could bring another Umbriel, the flying city the An-Xileel called down on Lilmoth with its mad Hist. The dreamers are people the order keeps in Fort Chalkmoth's cellar, fed sap and made to tell what the trees have seen. Cuts-the-Old-Knot told me what the Toh-Reel-Ka are: they see the marsh through sap-fed dreamers in Fort Chalkmoth's cellar, the moaning I heard. She seals trees to blind them, not to kill the trees. The healing I was sent to do would let the dreamers see again, and the stones in the order's hands would keep the Eye theirs. She wants the Eye lifted, which ends the dreams and kills many trees. This answers the question in my journal. Used where it sits, the Eye heals every tree and lets the dreamers see through them all; lifted, it parts the trees for good, about three in ten die, and the dreams end
plan.next: choose whether to fight her or believe her
plan.ways: fight: the hardest fight yet (she drinks her draught and fights as a battlemage); I get her spell tomes, robes, staff and draughts; I face the guardian alone; at the Eye I can only use it or take it. Believe: she waits in the hall beyond the gate and fights the guardian beside me; at the Eye I can use it, take it, or give it to her. Using the Eye with her alive kills her
